name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,642

clue.text: Welcome posh, kinky sex when drunk in a yard

indicators.note: kinky means twisted or bent out of the normal shape, so these letters are bent into a new order
to sit in something is to be enclosed by it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
IT is a long-standing euphemism for sex
taken as written
lit is slang for drunk
Y is the standard abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A racy invitation to drunken goings-on in someone's back yard.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex is an old euphemism, and lit is slang for drunk; 'when' simply joins the pieces in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitality is the friendly reception given to guests, the same idea as a warm greeting offered on arrival.

clue.text: Collect long pass from quarterback

blocks.note: first meaning: a collect is a short prayer, and this is a well-known Catholic one
second meaning: in American football, a desperate long throw downfield

explanation.surface: A quarterback collects the ball from a long pass.
explanation.walkthrough: Collect looks like a verb meaning gather; here it is the noun, a short liturgical prayer, stressed on the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a familiar Catholic prayer, and American football borrowed it for a last-gasp throw needing divine help.

clue.text: Investigates LAPD as helicopter lands in a careless manner

indicators.note: to land something is to catch and hold it, so the run of words holds the answer within it

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word, two whole words, then the first letter of the last

explanation.surface: Police in Los Angeles are investigated as a helicopter lands sloppily.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals of LAPD make it look like a real acronym to decode; it is just four letters sitting in the middle of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and without care, so the adverb matches doing something carelessly.

clue.text: Dream of unlimited cider and malt?

indicators.note: without limits means without boundaries, so the outermost letters at each end are dropped

blocks.note: the word with its first and last letters removed
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A drinker's fantasy of endless cider and malt whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Unlimited reads as 'as much as you like' in the surface, but it strips the ends from both drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect state one hopes for, which is what a dream in the sense of aspiration means.

clue.text: Greed - adult weakness - possessing a Republican

indicators.note: to possess is to hold, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a vice is a moral weakness
taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A political sketch: greed as the grown-up failing of a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: A comes first, then VICE swallows A and R to give V-AR-ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, a direct synonym of greed and one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Huge chaps in semi getting knocked out

indicators.note: to be in something is to be surrounded by it, so one piece sits inside the other
something knocked out of shape has been battered into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: chaps are men
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Big blokes get beaten in a semi-final.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi in Britain is a semi-detached house or a semi-final; here it is just four letters rearranged as IMSE, with MEN placed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large in size or degree, a plain synonym for huge.

clue.text: Benchmark for Met officer's baton?

blocks.note: London's Metropolitan Police is known as Scotland Yard, or the Yard, so something of a Met officer is the Yard's
a baton is a stick; its first letter is shared with the possessive

explanation.surface: Asking what standard a London police officer's truncheon should meet.
explanation.walkthrough: A Met officer's baton could whimsically be the Yard's stick; run together, the possessive S doubles as the start of STICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard used for comparison or measurement, which is exactly what a benchmark is.

clue.text: Five, say, say five a day ideally?

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral five
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: The healthy-eating advice to have five portions a day, repeated for emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition of 'say' hides that the first one is wordplay and the second starts the definition. Five a day is the UK health campaign urging five portions of fruit and vegetables daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Veg is the casual British short form for vegetables, which public health advice says to eat in five daily portions.

clue.text: Crude newspaper; Liberal, upper-class, very revolting

indicators.note: a revolt is a turning over, so the string of pieces is turned to run the other way

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a low-quality newspaper
L is the usual abbreviation for Liberal
U denotes upper-class usage in British slang
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A complaint about a coarse newspaper that is liberal, posh and thoroughly disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolting looks like a description of the paper, but it turns the whole string round. U for upper-class comes from the old British U and non-U distinction in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar and crude both describe something coarse, lacking refinement or taste, so they are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Spring greens go mushy without nitrogen, Yankee admitted

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away
to be admitted is to be let inside, so a letter is put into the rest
to go mushy is to lose firm shape, so the letters lose their order and are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
Yankee is the NATO alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: Overcooked spring greens turning to mush.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring greens are a leafy vegetable, so 'Spring' seems tied to them; it is the definition. Drop N from the vegetables, add Y, and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically shoots water and steam into the air, so it is a type of spring.

clue.text: Cross ... Knut scores!

blocks.note: Knut is the setter, who refers to himself as I
to score something is to rate it

explanation.surface: A sports exclamation: a cross into the box, and Knut scores.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like a football pass but is the adjective meaning angry; the setter's name stands for the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, and cross is the everyday British word for annoyed or angry.

clue.text: Daily tram serving old Whitehall building

indicators.note: to serve something up is to dish it out in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A daily tram service passing an old government building in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries; the Admiralty building housed the old naval department there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiralty was the British naval ministry, and its historic headquarters still stands on Whitehall in London.

clue.text: Small piece of meat I sent back - it's just for decoration

indicators.note: to send something back is to move it further down the line, so a letter shifts towards the end

blocks.note: the French culinary spelling for a small round cut of meat, with its I moved two places later

explanation.surface: A diner returns a tiny piece of meat, complaining it is mere garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: The French spelling of the cut is the starting point; move its I two places later and the English word appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large ornamental disc, often worn on a chain, whose purpose is purely ornamental.

clue.text: Husband implicated in constant humiliation

indicators.note: to be implicated in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: constant means unchanging, the same
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband caught up in a scandal suffers endless humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: Constant reads as an adjective on humiliation but is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Shame is the painful feeling of disgrace, closely synonymous with humiliation.

clue.text: Badge old Knut has back to front?

indicators.note: the back of the string goes to its front, so the last letter moves to the start

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Knut is this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: A question about whether Knut has pinned his badge on the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Back to front would normally mean reversal; here it means only the back letter moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge worn to show support or awarded as a prize at shows.

clue.text: Sleeping partner stimulating dry debate

indicators.note: something stimulating stirs things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A business partner who is silent, set against a lively debate.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner in business is a silent investor; here it is taken literally as a bedtime companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Children sleep cuddling a soft toy bear, making it quite literally the partner they share their bed with.

clue.text: Check flow of water ebbing

indicators.note: the sea going out retreats the way it came in, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a tide is the flow of the sea

explanation.surface: Monitoring the flow of water as the tide goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebbing fits the water picture so neatly that it hides its job as the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to check it over and correct errors, so the verbs overlap in proofreading.

clue.text: Good boy, 11, carrying old lady's first flowers

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so one piece holds others inside it
first points to the opening letter of the word before it only

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lad is a boy
eleven written as Roman numerals
O is the abbreviation for old
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A well-behaved eleven-year-old brings his old lady her first flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 looks like a cross-reference to another clue in the grid, but it is simply eleven as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall garden plants with spikes of showy blooms, so they are an example of flowers.

clue.text: Can it turn off hose carrying C6?

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: hose means stockings or socks
C6 is the musical pitch a soprano reaches as her highest showpiece note

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gadget can shut off a hose carrying something labelled C6.
explanation.walkthrough: Hose looks like a garden pipe, but here it is the legwear sense. C6 is scientific pitch notation for the note often called top C.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is the valve that shuts off a water supply, so it is the device that can turn the flow off.

clue.text: Chap tempted by Mahdi Army every now and again?

indicators.note: now and again means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A man lured into joining an Iraqi militia, the Mahdi Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Mahdi Army suggests a news story; it is only the source of letters, read at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man was tempted by Eve with the forbidden fruit, making him the original tempted chap.

clue.text: People generally forget cup size on international swimwear

indicators.note: to forget something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: mankind is people in general
D is a bra cup size
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Most people don't bother with bra sizes when choosing global beachwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Cup size sounds like a whole measurement but gives one letter to remove; 'on' places the final letter after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A mankini is a skimpy one-piece men's sling swimsuit, notorious from the film Borat.

clue.text: Mark part of test

blocks.note: first meaning: a stain left by spilled writing fluid
second meaning: one of the images in the Rorschach psychological test

explanation.surface: A teacher marking one section of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark and test suggest school grading, but one is a smudge and the other a psychologist's ambiguous picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot of ink is a stain, and the Rorschach assessment shows patients symmetrical blots to interpret.

clue.text: Very powerful, breaking within ten seconds

indicators.note: breaking open a run of words exposes what lies inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A powerful sprinter breaking ten seconds for the hundred metres.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking ten seconds is the language of sprint records, which hides its job as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense means extreme in strength or degree, matching something very powerful.

clue.text: Heavyweight notorious rapper's whiskey (one gallon)

blocks.note: the Notorious B.I.G. was an American rapper
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W
I is the Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for gallon

explanation.surface: A famous rapper drinking a whole gallon of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavyweight sounds like a boxer, but it means an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is an influential, important figure, the same as a heavyweight in politics or business.

clue.text: Head of Gaming punches programmer - a guy sounding, like, 8

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
a punch goes into something, so one piece is driven inside another

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a coder writes computer programs

explanation.surface: A gamer lashing out at a software developer.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the answer to 8 Down, GEYSER, which in British speech sounds like geezer, slang for a man, especially an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: A codger is an elderly man, and geezer is British slang for a bloke, often an old one.

clue.text: Yellowish-white gold plant placed outside

indicators.note: something placed outside surrounds what lies within

blocks.note: ivy is a climbing plant
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gold-coloured pot plant set out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldic word for gold, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is the creamy off-white colour of elephant tusks, so it names a yellowish-white shade.

clue.text: Scored Dutch Open shock!

indicators.note: a shock jolts things out of place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports headline: a surprise score at the Dutch Open golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock reads as a noun in a headline, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To notch up a win or points is to achieve or record them, so scored is a fair past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Empty, Henry starts to pour extra Sugar Puffs

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, a word keeps only its outer shell of letters
the start of each word means its opening letter

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Henry, bowl empty, starts pouring more breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sugar Puffs is a British breakfast cereal brand; it is split here, with the first word giving a letter and the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff a product is to promote it with exaggerated praise, which is what hypes means as a verb.

clue.text: Footballer's girlfriend/model Annie taking on queen of German style

indicators.note: to model something is to shape it, so these letters are shaped anew
to take on is to take inside, so one letter goes within the others

blocks.note: WAGs, wives and girlfriends, is the British tabloid term for footballers' partners
taken as written, to be rearranged
R, for regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A footballer's model girlfriend called Annie posing as a queen of German fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Model looks like Annie's job, but it is the rearrangement signal; the queen goes into the reshuffled name.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagnerian describes the grand, epic manner of the German composer Richard Wagner.

clue.text: Petty Officer receiving stolen picture

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A naval officer caught handling a stolen painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Receiving stolen goods is a crime, so the surface reads as a charge; receiving is really the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photographic image, one kind of picture.

clue.text: Starter of grilled American river fish

indicators.note: a starter comes at the beginning, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter
A is the abbreviation for American
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A menu offering grilled American river fish as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter looks like a menu course; it picks out a first letter. American river fish could be the whole definition, but only fish is.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted predatory freshwater species found in North American rivers.

clue.text: Complain faulty air intakes letting in sulphur

indicators.note: something faulty is not in working order, so the letters are put out of order
to let something in is to admit it inside, so a letter is added within

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Grumbling that broken vents are letting in the smell of sulphur.
explanation.walkthrough: Sulphur smells of rotten eggs, which suits the definition's stink.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a stink is an idiom for making a loud fuss or protesting strongly, the same as to complain.
